text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager P1: eu-west-2 - elevated DNS timeouts and 5xx errors from embeddings service (route-table/NAT suspicion). Alert triggered by 5xx rate > 15% over 3m for model-inference-eu.
jamie: acknowledged, oncall here. probing now. tagging net oncall @sofia
sofia: oncall net. seeing lots of partial egress failures from private subnets in az-c. DNS lookups to our resolvers 10.0.2.2 are timing out, but EC2 instances still have IMDS reachability. suspicion: route table assoc got changed on a subset of private subnets -> some traffic going to the wrong NAT in another AZ that has restrictive NACLs.
jamie: timeline? any recent infra deploys/terraform runs in eu-west-2
infra-bot: Deploy 1940122301 applied by ops-deploy-ci: terraform apply on account:redwood-prod/stage: updated module:vpc -> aws_route_table_association[private-rt-azc] (plan: replace)
sofia: that matches. replacement of association for private-rt-azc at 12:11UTC. I can see association now points to rt-azb instead of rt-azc for a subset (private-subnet-3/4).
kevin: I'm seeing 502/503 in frontends too. Is this limited to embeddings or broader? logs show DNS errors when resolving model shard endpoints causing upstream errors.
maria: support: customers pinging about latency and failure in embeddings. I've flagged a few high-value customers. preparing incident page but need root cause + ETA.
jamie: quick mitigation options: 1) re-associate route table back to correct subnets (fast) 2) attach a temporary nat gateway in az-c and update route table to prefer it 3) open NACL/SGs in target NAT AZ (riskier)
sofia: re-association is lowest risk. I'll run the replace-route-table-association call. doing dry-check first.
sofia: running:
```
aws ec2 replace-route-table-association --association-id rtbassoc-07a1b2c3d4 --route-table-id rtb-0a1b2c3d4e --region eu-west-2
```
sofia: dry-check shows association-change will move private-subnet-4 back to private-rt-azc -> expected to restore correct NAT path. proceeding in 2m.
jamie: note: rolling this should be quick but we need to monitor DNS success rate and 5xx rate. @kevin can you open a synthetic probe to embeddings endpoints and tail the logs?
kevin: running continuous curl/req test now. script:
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" "https://embeddings.eu-west-2.redwood/api/v1/encode" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" ; sleep 0.5; done
```
kevin: baseline was ~200ms 200s before, now see a lot of 5xx and many connection timeouts around DNS lookup.
infra-bot: Action: route-table association replace started by sofia at 12:18UTC (op-id rta-1940123456)
sofia: association replace done. verifying.
sofia: checking route table propagation in az-c -> private-subnet-3/4 both showing correct routes to nat-azc-01, target: 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-azc-01
kevin: retesting probes. immediate improvement: many 200s returning. 5xx rate dropping from 18% -> 3% in the first 60s.
jamie: :tada: seems to be improving. Maria, please tell support to mark impact as partial and notify affected customers with ETA "service degradation mitigated, monitoring". Draft comms and I'll sign off.
maria: drafting now. Copy: "We've mitigated a routing mis-association affecting a subset of eu-west-2 private subnets which caused DNS and downstream 5xx errors for embeddings. We're monitoring — we'll update in 30m."
sofia: note for postmortem: root cause likely was terraform plan that replaced association; plan didn't detect that association resource variable referenced wrong subnet id due to drift. We'll add guardrails.
jamie: running a quick check for NACL anomalies in azb target NAT to ensure no residual misconfig. `aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-xxxx`
sofia: NACLs in azb have a DENY on ephemeral high ports for that NAT due to a previous lockdown change. that explains why when some subnets pointed to that NAT they experienced egress hangs.
kevin: follow-up action: 1) add pre-deploy check that ensures route-table association target matches subnet AZ 2) add drift alert for rtbassoc resources 3) add quick rollback playbook in runbook.
jamie: agreed. assigning to sofia for infra guardrail, kevin for runbook updates, maria for customer comms.
sofia: I'll create terraform PR to prevent association replacement without explicit az-check and add terraform plan guard in CI. ETA PR by EOD.
kevin: I'll update runbook and add a short cli helper to scan for mismatched route-table associations across AZs.
maria: published initial customer note to affected accounts. support queue informed.
jamie: oncall handoff: my shift ends at 12:40UTC. handing to @kevin for next 12h window. kevin, you're oncall owner now.
kevin: acknowledged, taking oncall. monitoring dashboards for next 30m.
infra-bot: Monitoring: DNS success rate in eu-west-2 private subnets - now 98.7% (was 81%). 5xx rate for embeddings dropping to 2.1%.
jamie: closing timeline: 12:11UTC terraform replace started, 12:18UTC association fixed, 12:20UTC noticeable recovery, 12:30UTC majority traffic restored. impact window ~9 minutes of peak error, wider degradation 12:11-12:30.
sofia: root cause synopsis for postmortem: human-initiated terraform replacement of route-table-association moved a subset of private subnets to a route table that pointed at a NAT in another AZ with restrictive NACLs. combination caused DNS timeouts and 5xx.
kevin: mitigation steps completed and owner assignments noted. I'll open the postmortem doc and link runbook/PRs.
maria: adding affected customer list to postmortem and sending follow-up note once final verification done.
jamie: closing thread for now, will leave incident channel open for any regression. great work team. :heart:
